classification.notes: The paper defines one model: the 331 gauge extension with one fixed field content (three scalar triplets, two quark triplets plus one anti-triplet, three lepton anti-triplets, right-handed singlets for u, d, D/S/T, e, E) and one Lagrangian (Eqs. 2.8-2.9, 2.32, 2.54, 2.60-2.62). The parameter beta only sets the U(1)X and electric charges of the new states. This is the 'one-parameter family of U(1) charges' case in the definition, so it is single-model. The four benchmarks beta = +-sqrt(3), +-1/sqrt(3) are parameter points, not separate models. The scored reference 331.fr keeps beta general (external parameter Bet), so it matches the paper's Sec. 2 directly and covers all four benchmarks. It adds no fields beyond the paper; ghosts and Goldstones are gauge-fixing content (Feynman gauge), not new physics. Confusion risk is medium, not low, for two reasons. First, the abstract and text call the four beta choices 'benchmark 331 models' and 'different versions', so an agent may hard-code one beta value with integer charges (as the sibling files do) instead of the general-beta form the reference uses; field names and Q/X values would then differ from 331.fr. Second, the paper lists Feynman rules in unitary gauge (Appendix A) while the reference uses Feynman gauge with ghosts. Neither choice changes the field content or symmetry, so the model itself is the same. Naming differences: the reference calls the eta triplet Phi and the rho vev v (paper: v1).

refute_physics.reason: I re-read Sec. 2 of arXiv:1611.09337 and counted the models myself before I compared with the classifier. The paper defines one gauge group (SU(3)C x SU(3)L x U(1)X), one fixed field content, and one Lagrangian. The field content is: three scalar triplets rho, eta, chi (Eq. 2.2); quark triplets q1L, q2L and anti-triplet q3L with new quarks D, S, T (Eq. 2.56); three lepton anti-triplets (e, -nu, E) with new leptons E_l (Eq. 2.58); and right-handed singlets. The Lagrangian is Eqs. (2.8)-(2.9), (2.32), (2.54), (2.60)-(2.62). The parameter beta enters only through Q = T3 + beta T8 + X (Eq. 2.5), which fixes the U(1)X charges (Eq. 2.6) and the electric charges of the new states (Eqs. 2.7, 2.57, 2.59, Table 1). The four values beta = +-sqrt(3), +-1/sqrt(3) come from the requirement of integer charges plus positive M_Z'^2 (Eqs. 2.65-2.66). No beta value adds or removes a field, changes a representation, or changes a term in the Lagrangian. Table 1 lists the same particle rows (D, S, T, E_l, V, Y, H^QV, H^QY, H^+-) for all four beta values. This is exactly the 'one-parameter family of U(1) charges' case, which the definition counts as single-model. The paper does not use the classic minimal-331 lepton triplet (nu, e, e^c) or a scalar sextet for beta = sqrt(3); it keeps the same heavy-lepton E_l for every beta, so there is no distinct field-content alternative. The words 'four benchmark 331 models' and 'different versions' in the abstract and intro refer to the four beta points, not to different field content. The scored reference 331.fr keeps beta as an external parameter (Bet) and its 58 field classes are identical to the four fixed-beta sibling files; the siblings differ only in numeric charges, particle-name labels, and hard-coded parameter values (341 diff lines with 331_-1.fr, all of that kind). The reference is not a superset: ghosts and Goldstones are Feynman-gauge content, not new physics. Verdict: single_model = true, n_models = 1. The classifier's claim is supported.

classification.notes: The paper studies one model at collider energies: the SM plus one neutral massive vector X with dimension-4 anomaly-induced couplings to ZZ, Zgamma and WW. Two free couplings c1 and c2 control these vertices. The heavy fermion sectors are derivations, not alternatives: Sec. 2 gives a toy U(1)_A x U(1)_B model (Table 1), Sec. 3 a toy U(1)_Y x U(1)_X model with 4 Dirac fermions (Tables 2-3), and Sec. 4 a realistic SU(2) x U(1)_Y x U(1)_X charge assignment (Tables 4-5). All heavy states sit above 10 TeV and never enter the phenomenology of Sec. 5, so I count them as one model with a UV explanation. Reference file issues: (1) It has no Lagrangian at all, only M$ClassesDescription and M$Parameters, so any Lagrangian-level scoring against it is ill-defined. (2) It uses three independent couplings cW, cZ, cZgamma. The paper uses two: c1 fixes XZZ and XZgamma with a fixed ratio (sin theta_w / 2 vs cos theta_w), and c2 fixes XWW. (3) It adds Cmu, an X-muon coupling. The paper states SM fermions are neutral under U(1)_X, so this is a sector the paper never defines. This is why reference_is_superset is true, although the reference is a minimal file, not a large library. Confusion risk is medium: an agent that reads only the paper will get the field content right (one self-conjugate massive vector), but it will likely name and count the couplings as c1, c2 (not cW, cZ, cZgamma, Cmu), and it may try to implement the Stueckelberg field theta_X or the Sec. 4 heavy fermions and Phi as explicit fields.

classification.notes: The paper has two layers. Section II is a catalog of EFT operators for color sextets (not a model: generic hypercharges, ~100 operators). Section III picks the 3⊗6⊗8 invariant and defines two simplified models: a sextet fermion model (eq. 12, with up- and down-type copies Ψu, Ψd) and a sextet scalar model (eq. 13, with Φu, Φd). The paper calls them 'two simplified models' but presents all four fields together in Table X and implements them together in FeynRules. The sectors do not couple to each other, so the union is one consistent Lagrangian. The benchmark reference (by co-author T. Murphy) is exactly this union: four fields with the Table X charges and lepton numbers, kinetic terms, and the eq. (12)/(13) operators built with J^{sia} = -i√2 L t3 K̄ per eq. (A18) (K6, T, K3bar). No |H|^2 operator, no diquark (3⊗3⊗6bar) operators, no extra fields: not a superset. Cutoffs Λ are absorbed into the couplings (CFu etc.); Λ is not a separate parameter. Confusion risk is medium: (a) an agent could implement only the fermion sector or only Ψu, since the abstract says 'a model' and the phenomenology and Fig. 6 focus on Ψu, while the scalars are 'neglected so far'; (b) an agent could over-implement operators from Tables VIII/IX (e.g. the |H|^2 G term or diquark couplings); (c) the J^{sia} tensor must be built from FeynRules' K6/K3 objects, which is an implementation trap rather than a model-choice trap. The most natural reading of Table X plus 'We implement these simplified models' leads to the reference's four-field content, so most agents should converge on it. If the orchestrator prefers to treat a decoupled union that the authors implemented as one file as a single model, this page can be reclassified as single-model with n_models=1; the field content is unambiguous either way.

classification.notes: The paper is a single general model: all five scalar leptoquark representations added to the SM at once with the complete renormalizable Lagrangian. It offers no alternative representations, benchmark models, or EFT-vs-UV choice. The reference SLQrules.fr is the authors' own model file and implements exactly this model; it is not a superset. The reference weinberg_NLO.fr implements form (b) exactly: one field N1, six real Wilson coefficients plus Lambda, internal mN1, and Lagrangian terms that match Eqs. (23)-(29) including the G+G+ l^c PL l' contact term (coefficient gw^2 mN/(4 MW^2) = 2 x gw^2 mN/(8 MW^2)). classification.notes: The paper (Alwall et al. 2006, 'Is Vtb ~ 1?') is a multi-model paper. It defines two alternatives with different field content: (1) one vector-like SU(2)_L singlet up-type quark t' whose W/Z/H couplings all follow from one mixing angle theta and one mass (Eqs. 5-16); (2) a full chiral fourth generation t', b' with a unitary 4x4 CKM parametrized by three angles (Eq. 31), plus a remark that fourth-generation leptons are needed for anomaly cancellation. It also mentions in passing a vector-like singlet b' variant (Eq. 17) and dismisses it. The benchmark reference VLQ.fr is not an implementation of this paper. It is the 2013 model-independent top-partner library (arXiv:1305.4172): four vector-like quarks X(5/3), T(2/3), B(-1/3), Y(-4/3), each with generic left- and right-handed couplings to W, Z, H for all three SM generations, parametrized by kappa, zeta and branching-ratio inputs; SM couplings are not modified by mixing. X, Y and B never appear in the paper, and the paper's cos^2(theta) suppression of Ztt and the theta-derived coupling relations are not in the reference. The second reference file VLQ_Chromomagnetic.fr adds a chromomagnetic dipole operator (LChromoT, LChromoB with scale Lambda), which the paper also never defines. An agent that reads only the paper would write a 1-field t' singlet model with mixing angle theta, or a 2-quark fourth-generation model, and would not produce X(5/3) or Y(-4/3). The paper-to-reference pairing for this page looks mismatched; the reference belongs to a different arXiv paper.

refute_physics.reason: I re-read Section 2 of hep-ph/0607115 and counted the models before I compared with the classifier. The paper presents two distinct alternatives, not one model with limits. Model 1 (Sec. 2.1) adds one Q=+2/3 vector-like SU(2)_L iso-singlet quark t' (t'_L, t'_R both singlets). Its Lagrangian is the Yukawa plus Dirac mass terms of Eqs. (11)-(12). It gives a non-unitary 4x3 CKM (Eq. 6), tree-level FCNC Z and H couplings (Eqs. 14-16), and only two new parameters (theta, m_t'). Model 2 (Sec. 2.2) adds a full chiral fourth generation: an SU(2)_L doublet (t', b') with right-handed singlets, plus fourth-generation leptons for anomaly cancellation. It has a unitary 4x4 CKM with three angles (Eq. 31) and no tree-level FCNC. The two models differ in field content (b' present only in model 2), in SU(2) representation (singlet vs doublet), in symmetry structure (vector-like vs chiral), and in the Lagrangian (FCNC present vs absent, non-unitary 4x3 vs unitary 4x4). Neither is a limit or special case of the other. The paper itself frames them as two alternatives to be distinguished (intro line 79, Sec. 3.2 lines 1083 and 1102, conclusions line 1230). A vector-like b' singlet variant is mentioned in passing (line 216, Eq. 17) and dismissed; it is not developed and I do not count it. A strict reader could count it as a third model; this would not change single_model=false. The reference VLQ.fr is the 2013 Buchkremer-Cacciapaglia-Deandrea-Panizzi model-independent library with four VLQs X(5/3), T(2/3), B(-1/3), Y(-4/3) and generic kappa/zeta couplings. It is not an implementation of this paper. It is a superset in field content, but it also lacks the paper's modifications of SM couplings (cos^2 theta suppression of Ztt, cos theta rescaling of Vti), because it assumes mass and physical eigenstates match for the VLQs. The chiral fourth-generation model is not in the reference at all. The classifier's verdict (multi-model, n=2, reference mismatched) is supported by strong evidence, so I cannot refute it.

classification.notes: The paper defines one model: the minimal vector set {U1 ~ (3,1,2/3), Z' ~ (1,1,0), G' ~ (8,1,0)} with a single phenomenological Lagrangian (eqs. 9-11), flavour textures (eq. 13), and free non-minimal gauge couplings kappa_U, kappa~_U, kappa_G', kappa~_G'. Section 2 discusses gauge vs strongly-interacting UV completions only as motivation; no second Lagrangian is written. Parameter benchmarks (beta_R^33 in {0, 0.5, 1}, kappa_U in {0,1}, widths) are scans, not separate models. The benchmark scores against VLferm.fr, which is the wrong file for this paper. VLferm.fr is a 2022 add-on by Fuentes-Martin and Faroughy (Faroughy is not a paper author). It adds SU(2) doublet vector-like fermions chiL ~ (1,2,-1/2) and chiQ ~ (3,2,1/6) with couplings to U1, Z', G' and mixing terms to 2nd/3rd generation SM fermions. It is not standalone: it uses VLQ, Zp, Gp, gU, gZp, gGp, and newCKM, which are declared in the other three files. An agent that reads only the paper will write vector_LQ + Zprime + coloron content and will never produce Ln/Le/Qu/Qd, so a mismatch is near certain. Recommendation: re-point the LeptoQuark reference to the set {vector_LQ.fr, Zprime.fr, coloron.fr} (or concatenate them), and drop VLferm.fr from the scored reference.

classification.notes: The paper is a single-model paper. It defines one new charged vector W' with one Lagrangian (Eq. 1) and one parameter set (C^L, C^R matrices, or equivalently gL, gR, zeta, omega, V^L, V^R in Eq. 2). Purely left-handed, purely right-handed, lepton-decay-open vs closed, and the top-flavor example are limits or parameter points of the same model. The reference weff.fr (Fuks, FeynRules WEff model) is a one-to-one implementation of Eq. (1): gL/gR times C^L/C^R with Wp coupling to nu-l and u-d for all three generations, both chiralities, no W'-W-Z or W'-W-gamma couplings, no kinetic term written (FeynRules derives the propagator from the class declaration). The reference is not a superset. The main confusion risk is the right-handed neutrino: the abstract and Eq. (28) treat nuR as possibly massive (m = m_nuR), so an agent reading only the paper may add a heavy nuR field (2 new fields) or may drop the leptonic coupling for the closed-channel case, while the reference uses the massless SM neutrino with a right-handed projector. A second, minor risk is parameterization (Eq. 2 style gR cos zeta V^R, gL sin zeta V^L, CP phase omega) versus the reference's C^{L,R} plus kL, kR; this is physically equivalent. Reference default CRq values (CRq[1,1]=1, CRq[2,1]=0) differ from the paper's CKM choice Eq. (24), but that is a parameter value, not a model difference.

(28) is a generality of the cross-section formula for 'any final state', not an alternative field content offered for implementation. The paper is from 2002 and names no public model file (no mention of MadEvent, Pythia, FeynRules, or any code), so there is no paper-side statement about what a model file implements. The reference directory holds a single file, weff.fr, whose header says 'FeynRules model file: SM + Wprime', M$ModelName 'WEff', and cites Z. Sullivan PRD 66 075011 (the journal version of hep-ph/0207290). classification.notes: This is a CMS experimental search paper (model-independent limit), not a model-building paper. It uses two benchmark model classes with different field content: (1) NMSSM with h1/h2 and light pseudoscalar a1; (2) dark SUSY = MSSM plus a broken U(1)_D giving a dark photon gamma_D (kinetic mixing epsilon with the photon) and a dark neutralino nD. The paper defines neither model beyond decay topologies and mass points; it defers the model descriptions to Refs. [15] and [18]. The benchmark reference implements only the dark SUSY benchmark. The reference is a superset: it is the full FeynRules MSSM superfield implementation (squarks, sleptons, gluino, charginos, four neutralinos, 2HDM Higgs sector, soft terms, ghosts; 39 fields) plus the dark sector, whereas the paper's dark SUSY topology uses only h, n1, nD, gamma_D and muons. The reference also deviates from the paper's physics description: it has no kinetic-mixing parameter epsilon; instead it uses a direct vector coupling gd (=0.001) of AD to muons and a direct I*gd n1-nD-AD vertex, with the U(1)_D gaugino set to zero. An agent reading only the paper would have to choose between NMSSM and dark SUSY, would almost certainly write a simplified model (h, n1, nD, gamma_D, explicit h-n1-n1 coupling, epsilon F F_D kinetic mixing) rather than a full MSSM superfield file, and would not reproduce the reference's direct gd couplings. Confusion risk is therefore high.

refute_physics.reason: The classifier's verdict is supported. The paper (CMS-HIG-18-003, a model-independent 4-muon search) explicitly presents two benchmark model classes with different field content and symmetry structure: (1) the NMSSM, where h1 or h2 decays to a pair of light CP-odd singlet-like scalars a1; (2) dark SUSY, where the MSSM is extended by a broken U(1)_D that gives a dark photon gamma_D (kinetic mixing epsilon with the photon) and a dark neutralino nD, with h -> 2 n1 -> 2 nD + 2 gamma_D. These are alternatives an implementer must choose between; neither is a limit of the other. Everything else in the paper (h1 vs h2, the tan beta = 20 / B = 0.3% reference scenario, epsilon and m_gammaD and c-tau scans, mass points) is a parameter choice inside one of the two classes. The paper writes no Lagrangian, superpotential, or field table for either model and defers both to Refs. [15] and [18]. The benchmark reference MSSMD.fr implements only the dark SUSY class as the full FeynRules MSSM superfield model plus U1D, AD, neuD, a direct I*gd n1-nD-AD vertex, and a direct gd AD-mu-mu vertex, with no epsilon parameter and the U(1)_D gaugino set to zero. classification.notes:
Classification. The paper presents three alternative spin hypotheses (scalar X0, vector X1, tensor X2) for one observed boson, each with its own Lagrangian L_J (eq. 2.1). The task definition lists 'spin-0 vs spin-1 vs spin-2' alternatives as multi-model, so n_models = 3. The 0+/0- and 1+/1- cases are parameter limits of the same field (alpha, eqs. 2.13-2.14), not separate models. The paper itself, however, calls the bundle one 'Higgs Characterisation model' and the reference implements all three fields in one file, so reference_implements = all-in-one.

Reference structure. HiggsCharacterisation.fr (v3.4, 17.10.2013, authors de Aquino and Mawatari) declares exactly the three paper fields X0 (PDG 5000000), X1 (5000001), X2 (5000002). It contains L0v (eq. 2.4 vector couplings, incl. the derivative kHda/kHdz/kHdw terms), L1 (eqs. 2.8, 2.11, 2.12 with kqa/kqb/kla/klb instead of the paper's kappa_fa/kappa_fb), and L2 (eqs. 2.15-2.16 with kq, kl, kg, ka, kz, kw). The Table 2 g couplings match (e.g. gHaa = 47 alpha/(18 pi v), gHgg = -alpha_s/(3 pi v)).

Superset caveats (minor, so flag set false). (a) L0v6: an effective gg X0 X0 vertex (kHHgg, kAAgg) added in v3.3 after the paper; the paper only says four-point operators are 'work in progress'. (b) Gauge-fixing terms TGFg/TGFa in the spin-2 E-M tensor, a MadGraph technicality the paper does not mention. (c) Full SM E-M tensors (W charged currents, MZ^2/MW^2 mass terms, Yukawa mass terms TYq/TYl) that the paper only cites from refs. [46, 48].

Why confusion risk is high. (1) The scored file omits eq. (2.2) (X0 Yukawa) and the kappa_SM ZZ/WW term; these are realised in the companion SM_HC.fr by renaming the SM Higgs to X0 (Phi[2] -> (vev + ca X0 + I G0)/Sqrt[2]) and inserting kSM, kHtt, kAtt etc. An agent reading only the paper will most likely write all of eqs. (2.2) and (2.4) into its new-physics file and keep or drop the SM Higgs H on its own judgement. (2) The paper gives only the QED E-M tensor; the spin-2 sector must be reconstructed from external references. (3) An agent may split the three spins into separate files or implement only one hypothesis. Field content (3 fields) is explicit in the paper, so the mismatch is mostly in Lagrangian placement and spin-2 details rather than in particle content.

Other reference files. HC.fr is v4.1 (2016) of the same all-in-one model with added kq3, X2-Z-A and X0 contact terms. HiggsCharacterization.fr is v2.0 (April 2013, pre-paper) with a different field list (X1, X1p, X0x, X2) and higher-dimension spin-2 operators the paper dropped. SM_HC.fr and SM_HC3.fr are the modified SM (Higgs renamed X0) that the HC files import as LSM.

classification.notes: The paper defines one model. It is the L+N vector-like confinement model with Yukawa couplings to the elementary Higgs. The low-energy theory is a chiral Lagrangian (eqs. 6-8) with a pion triplet pi3, a composite doublet K2, and a singlet eta. The K2-H mixing gives a type-I 2HDM. The V+L variant is only named once. The relaxion section (Sec. 4) reuses the same model and adds only an axion-like coupling to the SU(N) gluons; it does not define a second full model. The reference file does not match this paper. Its header names Barducci, Redi, Tesi (May 2018). It implements a collider-vertex file: pion triplet with W couplings and the anomaly term (N=3, f_pi = m_rho/g_rho), plus a rho vector triplet with rho-fermion and rho-pi-pi couplings that the paper never writes. It is a superset in the rho sector and a subset elsewhere: no K2 doublet, no eta, no K2-H mixing, no CP phases, no relaxion. An agent that reads only the paper will most likely write pi3 + K2 + eta with Higgs mixing and anomaly terms, and no rho. This is a very different field content from the reference. The anomaly normalization in the reference also appears to differ by a factor 2 from eq. (26) (no 1/2 from the dual tensor).
